issues.issue: The two printed columns have run together, so the 3.a. weather-conditions exclusion is interleaved with the freezing and dishonesty exclusions and paragraph 3.c. breaks off at "described premises" without its ensuing-loss exception.

Sub-paragraph (4)(a) excludes increased loss from delay in rebuilding caused by "interference at the location ... by strikers or other persons", and the catch-all "or other persons" against the single specific "strikers" leaves the exclusion's reach open; "(6) Any other consequential loss" is a second unbounded catch-all.

The exclusion of loss from delay in rebuilding must be read against the "period of restoration" definition (c240), which itself measures the loss period by when property "should be repaired, rebuilt or replaced with reasonable speed".
It disapplies an exclusion for the Leasehold Interest Coverage Form, which is not among the forms scheduled in this policy's Declarations.
It operates on the Leasehold Interest Coverage Form, which this policy does not include.
It operates on the Legal Liability Coverage Form, which is not scheduled in this policy's Declarations.
It adds exclusions to the Legal Liability Coverage Form, a form this policy does not contain.
"[A]n abrupt falling down or caving in" with the result that the building "cannot be occupied for its intended purpose" leaves the degree of structural failure required unspecified.

The paragraph runs into unrelated text at the end ("even if use of ocd 2 live material of methods, In construct remodeling or renovation, contributes to tt collapse"), so limb f. is not legible as written.

The entry begins with a duplicate of paragraph 2.f. and the sentence "The criteria set forth in 1.a. through 1.d. do af tt loss listed In 2.a., 2.d. and 2.e." is incomplete, so the rule for outdoor property cannot be read.

The prerequisite that "all reasonable means were used to save and preserve the property from further damage" is an unmeasured standard, and the reference to "E.2. and E.6." does not match the paragraph numbering that follows.

Three different provisions — the fungus Business Income limb, the Property In Transit extension and the Water Damage extension — are interleaved line by line, so neither the 30-day fungus sub-limit nor its conditions can be read continuously.
The entry opens with stray fungus/period-of-restoration text before the Glass extension begins, so the provision's own opening words are absent.

The endorsement deletes "the second and third paragraphs" of Civil Authority and substitutes a single sentence, but it does not say which of the printed paragraphs those are or what becomes of the 72-hour waiting period and the Extra Expense limb.
As printed, the Civil Authority Additional Coverage (c197) does not have the paragraph structure this endorsement assumes, so it cannot be applied to that clause without reconstruction.

The substituted paragraph a. makes the period of restoration begin "[i]mmediately after the time of direct physical loss", collapsing the printed form's separate start dates for Business Income and for Extra Expense into one.
It contradicts paragraph a. of the "Period of Restoration" definition in the Business Income form (c240), which begins Business Income coverage only 72 hours after the loss.
"Continuing normal operating expenses incurred, including payroll" does not say which expenses continue or how they are separated from expenses that cease when the building is destroyed.

The whole clause turns on which option "is selected" in the Declarations, but the Declarations entry (c004) reads "BLANKET BUSINESS INCOME RENTAL ... PROP INCL EXTRA EXPENSE" and selects none of a., b. or c.

The promise is to pay "the actual loss of Business Income you sustain due to the necessary 'suspension' of your 'operations' during the 'period of restoration'", and both "actual loss ... you sustain" and "necessary" suspension are left undefined as measures of recovery.

The length of the recovery is fixed entirely by the "period of restoration" definition (c240) as amended by the CP 15 56 endorsement (c185), and those two provisions do not give a single answer for a destroyed apartment building.

"[N]ecessary expenses you incur during the 'period of restoration' that you would not have incurred" is qualified by "[a]void or minimize" the suspension, without any standard for measuring necessity.
The CP 15 56 endorsement (c184) purports to delete the second and third paragraphs of this coverage and substitute a single sentence, which cannot be mapped onto the paragraphs printed here.

The extended period begins only when property "is actually repaired, rebuilt or replaced and 'operations' are resumed" and ends when the insured "could restore" income "with reasonable speed", a standard the clause does not define.

The Extended "Rental Value" text is interleaved with the Interruption Of Computer Operations paragraphs, so the sentence beginning "lf the necessary 'suspension' of your 'operations' produces a 'Rental Value' loss" is split from its own conclusion.

Its trigger — the date property "is actually repaired, rebuilt or replaced and tenantability is restored" — has to be reconciled with the "period of restoration" definition (c240), which ends when property merely "should be repaired".
